findings.title: WorkflowNavigator's three "in-scope" sites are the SliceStatus.status sites TD-3 excludes
findings.description:
The scope table (line 36) classifies `WorkflowNavigator.ts`'s 3 sites as `NormalizedStatus` `=== 'complete'` checks, the component table (line 75) and migration step 4 (line 90) sweep them — but verified against source, all three are members of the `SliceStatus.status` workflow-position union (types.ts:267–274), not `NormalizedStatus`:

- `WorkflowNavigator.ts:312` and `:345` — `slice.status === 'complete'` where `slice` is `status.activeSlice: SliceStatus`
- `WorkflowNavigator.ts:588` — `return { ...base, status: 'complete', taskProgress }` constructing a `SliceStatus` (`base: SliceStatus` in `deriveSliceStatus`)

This directly contradicts TD-3 (slice doc lines 104–106: "`SliceStatus.status` … is a different, larger union … touching it risks conflating two independent unions. Left untouched.") and the success criterion at line 136 ("`SliceStatus.status` remain untouched … not accidentally swept"). Executing step 4 as written violates the design's own exclusion; skipping it makes WorkflowNavigator's true in-scope count 0 and leaves 3 pattern matches that defeat the "zero matches in the six swept files" check at line 135. Reconcile by dropping the WorkflowNavigator row and migration step 4 (and adjusting the success-grep expectations), since the sweep of `NormalizedStatus` sites is complete without them — not by amending TD-3, whose reasoning is correct.

findings.title: Verification counts and the success grep don't fully reconcile with the code
findings.description: Minor count inaccuracies in the site table and Verification Walkthrough (all hedged as "~65"/"~75", so informational): `statusNormalizer.ts`'s value side is 14 occurrences (lines 5–18), not 13; the walkthrough's after-count of "SliceStatus.status (4)" matches only 1 occurrence under the stated pattern (`types.ts:269`, the sole `'complete'`); and `ConsistencyChecker.ts`'s "36 sites" includes 3 literal occurrences inside the comment at `ConsistencyChecker.ts:514` (`// 'complete' | 'in-progress' | 'not-started'`), which the success grep will match. That comment documents the pre-TD-1 type and is stale after the retype, so the sweep should update it (and the similar comment at `ProjectModelBuilder.ts:179`) or the grep at line 135 needs to be comment-aware — as written, "zero matches in the six swept files" is unachievable while the comment stands. (Also trivial: `ProjectModelBuilder.ts`'s `'unknown'` literal is at line 181, plus 256/269/270 — not "line 179" — though the exclusion conclusion is unchanged.)

findings.title: Scope, proportionality, and architecture alignment hold
findings.description: The slice fits the 900-arch scope ("pattern consolidation", "hard-coded values → constants") and its principles: a themed slice with clear success criteria, no behavior change, with the existing test suite run before/after as the regression guard the "No behavior changes without tests" principle requires (the design states the test baseline explicitly: 931/934 core, 428/432 cli, 184/184 mcp). No new components, helpers, or abstractions — matching "resist adding complexity". The exclusions are verified as correct, not scope-dropping: `frontmatterSchema.ts`'s `VALID_STATUSES` is a distinct raw-token vocabulary including `deferred` (which `statusNormalizer.ts:26`'s own comment confirms has no `NormalizedStatus` counterpart), and `STATUS_MAP`'s keys are alias inputs. Slice-plan entry 910's assigned scope is covered; the single addition (TD-1's one-line retype of `TaskFileResult.inferredStatus`) removes a duplicate definition of the same three values and directly serves the plan's stated purpose, so it is not scope creep. The NFR-restate and failure-mode-enumeration criteria are N/A — the parent architecture states no latency/throughput NFRs, and the slice adds no I/O paths or message types; its one real failure mode (an intermediate non-building state between the retype and its producer's sweep) is explicitly handled by coupling them in migration step 1.

findings.title: TD-1's type widening is safe for all consumers; dependency direction is correct
findings.description: Verified every `inferredStatus` consumer (`ArtifactIntrospector.ts:122`, `WorkflowNavigator.ts:574/659`, `ConsistencyChecker.ts:286/325/352/392`, `taskFileParser.ts:60–76`): all use `===` comparisons or pass the value through to `NormalizedStatus`-typed fields (`types.ts:276/321`); no exhaustive `switch` exists that the widened union would break. TD-1's claim that nothing validates `inferredStatus` excludes `'deprecated'` holds. Dependencies point correctly inward: the slice consumes `STATUS` from `introspection/types.ts` (already imported with the value+type pattern in `statusDerivation.ts:1` and `WorkflowNavigator.ts:13`, confirming the "already imports `STATUS`" note), provides nothing, and leaves the exported `NormalizedStatus` type unchanged so CLI/MCP consumers are unaffected — matching the design's "no public API signature changes" claim.
